data.reasoning: This is a standard AUR binary package that downloads pre-built binaries from the official GitHub releases (topgrade-rs/topgrade) with pinned b2sum checksums for integrity verification. The PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments and a standard package() function that installs the binary and generates documentation (manpage, shell completions) by executing the verified binary. No malicious code, obfuscation, unexpected network requests, or injection patterns are present. The only 'disagreement' was a tool error (HTTP 400) in one report when auditing .SRCINFO, which is metadata-only and doesn't execute code.
data.disagreement_analysis: The inconclusive result from qwen3-235b was caused by an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when auditing .SRCINFO, not a substantive security finding. The PKGBUILD was successfully reviewed and deemed safe. The other two reports (deepseek-v4-flash and openrouter/free) both correctly identified the package as safe. Since openrouter/free is marked advisory:true, it doesn't count as a vote, but its analysis aligns with deepseek-v4-flash.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to audit .SRCINFO due to HTTP 400 API error, but .SRCINFO is metadata-only and doesn't affect security verdict
learnings: Tool errors on non-executable metadata files (.SRCINFO) should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict when executable files (PKGBUILD) are successfully audited and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between 'failed to review due to error' and 'reviewed and found issues' when computing final verdicts
For simple -bin packages with pinned checksums and standard installation patterns, models should be more confident in safe verdicts when no injection patterns are detected
